title: Parametric, nonparametric, linear
summary: What is fixed about a model: its parameter count, and whether it is linear in those parameters.

choices.text: Linear discriminant analysis is supervised. It uses class labels to choose a separating projection; the usual form models classes as Gaussians that share one covariance.
Linear regression and logistic regression are parametric: once the features are chosen, a weight vector of fixed length summarizes the fit.
k-nearest neighbors is nonparametric. The predictor stores the training rows, so what you keep grows with the sample.
"Linear" means linear in the parameters. Expanding each row with squares and products, then running least squares, is still linear in the weights.
A decision tree whose depth is not capped has a parameter count fixed before any row is seen, the same way logistic regression does.
A multilayer network with a nonlinear activation between the weight layers is nonlinear. It does not collapse to one weight vector on a feature map you fixed before training.
